info.title: Entur journey notification notification API
info.summary: Register a commuter's recurring journey; receive a signed webhook when a disruption is predicted to hit it.
info.description:
The authenticated surface a client BFF manages its own commuter registrations through, plus the outbound event contract under `webhooks` below.

**This document renders the two authored schemas rather than restating them.** `subscription.schema.json` and `event.schema.json` sit beside this file and every property here is a `$ref` into one of them: two definitions of one payload is how they drift, and the client's TypeScript types are generated from this document. OpenAPI 3.1 is JSON Schema 2020-12, so the references resolve without translation.

**One property is inline rather than a `$ref`, on purpose:** `TestEventRequest.subscription_id`. A create body must carry your own reference and nothing else, while `POST /test-events` additionally accepts the opaque `subscription_id` an event carries -- so the two are genuinely different constraints, and referencing the stricter create-side one would publish a schema that refuses a value this API had itself just served. Widening the shared definition to match would be the same mistake pointing the other way.

**Two operations are public.** `GET /journey-alerts` reads the alert state on a journey definition nobody registered -- what the Entur app's favourites panel asks for a saved route -- and `GET /journey-status` grades every train in that definition's window today. Both take no credential, share one limiter, and declare `security: []` on themselves; everything else below is authenticated as described next.

**Authentication** is a bearer credential this app issued: `Authorization: Bearer <key-id>.<secret>`. The `key-id` is prefixed `kixn_`; the secret is 256 random bits, shown once at issue and stored here only as an HMAC-SHA256 hash under a pepper. Never a cookie: the app serves one global CORS policy allowing every origin, so a cookie would be sent from all of them. Several credentials are live at once, which is how rotation works -- a new `key-id` is issued, the client cuts over, and the old one is revoked afterwards, so nothing is taken down for a rotation.

**Ownership comes from the credential.** Every route acts on the authenticated client's own records only, and `client_id` in a request body is ignored. A record belonging to another client is indistinguishable from one that does not exist: both are 404, and no response body names anything about another client.

**Statuses worth knowing before you write a client.** `401` is a credential problem and carries no detail about which; `403` means the client is suspended, which is a conversation with an operator rather than a credential to rotate; `429` is a limiter tier or a quota ceiling and always carries a bounded `Retry-After`; `503` means this deployment has no webhook channel configured, or its store is briefly unavailable -- both retryable, neither a statement about your credential (on the public read it means the prediction cache is not loaded yet, which is the minute after a deploy).

**`422` has two body shapes, and the one you will meet first is the array.** A refusal this application made carries a string `detail` (`Error`); a refusal the framework made before any handler ran carries an array of objects (`ValidationError`) -- an out-of-range `limit`, an unknown body property, a `pattern` violation, a missing required property, an over-long path segment. Those are the errors you hit while writing the client, so branch on `detail`'s type rather than assuming a string. Every documented `422` here says which shapes it can be.

**Retention.** A subscription expires at the earlier of 180 days from creation and 60 days from your last interaction with it, and both horizons are enforced when it is read as well as by the store's own expiry -- so a subscription never keeps alerting past its published expiry. Events and delivery records are kept 7 days. A `DELETE` tombstones the subscription in one write that stops routing and then deletes its events, deliveries and alert subjects; where that has not completed the response says so and names the maximum residual window, after which expiry removes the remainder.

servers.description: Test (tst). Records and credentials are per environment; a production credential is not valid here.

tags.name: notification-journey-alerts
tags.description: The public, credential-free reads on a journey definition nobody registered -- what the Entur app's favourites panel asks for a saved route: the alert-worthy trains ahead (`journey-alerts`) and every train in today's window, graded (`journey-status`). The only two operations in this document with `security: []`.

post.summary: Create or replace a watch by your own reference
post.description:
Idempotent on (reference, definition): an identical retry returns the stored record and changes nothing but the inactivity horizon, so an unacknowledged POST is safe to repeat. A different definition under the same reference amends it and bumps `version`. A reference that has been deleted is **not** resurrected -- the id is spent and its record is the audit trail -- which is a 409.

The window, the weekday set and the stop pair are validated exactly as Entur's own Smarte reisevarsler validates them, including a window over midnight: `begin` and `end` must differ, and an `end` before `begin` is one window from `begin` until `end` the next morning, belonging to the weekday it begins on (`days: [4]` is Friday night into Saturday). A watch registered as two halves before this keeps working unchanged.

A stop pair that no direct trip serves is **stored, never refused** -- weekend-only and seasonal routes are why a refusal would be wrong -- and carries the caveat on `servable` with `servable_checked_at` beside it.

`servable` is **null on this response**, always: the question is a BigQuery job and this API exists to onboard an existing commuter base, so a background sweep establishes it within the hour instead of asking on the registration path. Null means "not established" and must never be rendered to a traveller as an all-clear.

`alerts` is **null** on this response: a create or replace does not read the alert state. Null therefore means "not included here", never "no standing alerts" -- that is `n_active: 0` with `truncated: false`, from either GET route.

parameters.name: If-Match
parameters.description: The `version` you last read. A mismatch is 409 rather than a silent overwrite. Omit it to replace unconditionally.

200.description: The watch already existed: unchanged (an identical retry) or amended.

409.description: The reference is tombstoned, or `version` moved under you.

get.description:
Oldest first. The set is bounded by the per-client ceiling on active subscriptions, so paging is a slice of one bounded read: pass a page's `next_cursor` back as `after`. A cursor the current set no longer contains is a 400 rather than an empty page, because "that watch is gone" and "nothing matched" are different answers.

Each watch carries `alerts`: its **current alert state**, read from the notification service's own committed alert subjects rather than re-evaluated, so it is what stands right now about this watch. `n_active` counts standing alerts (withdrawn ones are not standing and are not listed), `n_confirmed` how many are confirmed cancellations, and `subjects` carries the worst few -- capped at the number of notifications one watch can receive in an Oslo day, because a longer list would enumerate what that cap has already suppressed. **Read `truncated`.** When it is true the counts are lower bounds and `n_active: 0` means "we could not establish this", never "all clear". A list page reads every row's state in ONE query, so a bounded read marks *every* row truncated -- including rows whose own subjects fitted, because a watch crowded out of the page would otherwise read exactly like a calm one. Ask about that watch individually and the read is scoped to it alone.

parameters.name: subscription_id
parameters.description: Your own reference. The opaque `subscription_id` an event carries is also accepted, so a receiver holding an event can look the watch up without knowing how records are keyed.

get.summary: One watch, with servability and freshness
get.description:
Missing, deleted, expired and belonging to another client are all 404: one answer for four states, so the difference cannot be used to enumerate anything.

Each watch carries `alerts`: its **current alert state**, read from the notification service's own committed alert subjects rather than re-evaluated, so it is what stands right now about this watch. `n_active` counts standing alerts (withdrawn ones are not standing and are not listed), `n_confirmed` how many are confirmed cancellations, and `subjects` carries the worst few -- capped at the number of notifications one watch can receive in an Oslo day, because a longer list would enumerate what that cap has already suppressed. **Read `truncated`.** When it is true the counts are lower bounds and `n_active: 0` means "we could not establish this", never "all clear".

delete.summary: Stop a watch: tombstone, then durable cleanup
delete.description:
Ordered and durable. The tombstone lands first, in one write that stops routing, and only then are the watch's events, deliveries and alert subjects removed -- reversed, a partial failure would leave a routable watch whose events were already gone.

Repeated deletion succeeds, and so does deleting a reference that never existed (`existed: false`). Where cleanup has not finished, `cleanup.state` is `pending` and a repeated `DELETE` resumes it; `cleanup.residual_hours` is the maximum window after which expiry removes whatever is left.

Deletion deliberately does not reach the notification wording caches: those key on the journey definition, which is exactly what this watch shares with any other registration on the same route, and they expire with the disruption they describe.

get.summary: Destination readiness and signing key ids
get.description:
Your provisioned callback, whether it is currently deliverable, and which signing generations are live. **Generation numbers only, never a secret**: a signing secret is derived from a root over `destination_id || generation` and is stored nowhere, and this endpoint never derives one.

`paused` is set automatically when your endpoint answers `410 Gone` -- the documented meaning of which is "stop sending" -- and is lifted only by an Entur operator. While it is paused, new watches can still be registered and events still queue; nothing is dialled.

404.description: No destination is provisioned for this client. An operator provisions one out of band.

post.summary: Send one signed synthetic event to your callback
post.description:
Signs and dials one synthetic event, so a receiver can be verified end to end before a real disruption. **Restricted to a subscription created with `test: true`**, and that marker is immutable -- changing it needs delete and re-create -- because it rides inside the signed body and a receiver is expected to refuse a test event before dispatching a native notification. Anything else is 409.

The event's `test` field, `event_id` and `alert_id` are unique per call, so asking twice gives two notifications rather than one the receiver's duplicate rule discards. Nothing is stored: no event, no delivery record, and your daily notification allowance is untouched.

Answers 200 with the outcome even when your endpoint rejected the attempt -- the classification is the diagnosis. A refusal on Entur's side is a 4xx or 503 as usual.

200.description: The attempt was made; the body says how it went.

409.description: The watch is not test-only, or the destination is missing or paused.

503.description: Signing is not configured in this deployment, or the store is unavailable.

get.summary: The alert-worthy trains ahead on a journey definition, right now
get.description:
What Entur's own Smarte reisevarsler would be warning about on this route, for a definition nobody registered: one entry per alert-worthy train ahead, soonest first, each carrying the webhook event's own `payload` -- the ready-to-display Norwegian notification, the figures, the contributing situations and the alternative journey. Built for a favourites panel: the app's BFF asks once per saved route when a user opens the app.

**No credential.** This is the one public operation in this document: `security: []` here overrides the global `clientKey`. A stop pair holds nothing personal, and the read has its own limiter -- a global ceiling of 300 reads a minute across every anonymous caller and 30 a minute per canonical stop pair -- which is `429 rate_limited` with `Retry-After: 60` when it binds. The ceiling and the read's wording and Journey Planner allowances are **shared by every anonymous caller**, the app's BFF included, with no reserved slice: treat a 429, and a `rate_limited` status on an entry, as ordinary states and serve your cached answer.

**The definition.** `from_stop` and `to_stop` are `NSR:StopPlace:<digits>` and are canonicalized as `/varsel` canonicalizes a submitted ref (a collapsed ref names the same place; two refs that collapse to one place are a 422). `begin`/`end` is an optional Oslo `HH:MM` period, both or neither, `begin` before `end`; `days` an optional repeated weekday parameter (`days=0&days=1`, 0 = Monday). No period means the whole day; no days means today's and tomorrow's weekday, which is every window the prediction cache can carry. The canonical definition and the windows asked about are echoed, so key your cache on `journey` plus `refreshed_at` and never on the query string you sent.

**Selection is the notification pass's, unchanged.** Which trains alert, which alerts clear the per-operator bar, the collapse of several situations about one train into one entry: all `/varsel`'s and the webhook channel's. So an empty `alerts` means *no alert-worthy train among the trains the service scores* -- direct trips by the operators in `coverage.operators` -- and never all-clear. A trip with a transfer never alerts, and nothing here is a claim about any other operator. One difference from the webhook channel: a Vy train missing from today's timetable altogether (usually on this weekday, not in today's plan, no cancellation published; situation `KIX:PlanRemoved:<journey_ref>`) is listed here as `confirmed`, and no webhook event is ever minted for one.

**Two halves, and a wait budget between them.** The figures -- which trains, which numbers -- are served at once from the service's in-process cache. The model's wording and the alternative journey are fetched on request, in the background, under the read's own allowances; the request waits up to `wait` seconds for them and then answers with whatever is ready. An entry that is not ready carries the template wording and no alternative, and its `wording.status` / `alternative.status` say why. `complete` is true only when every listed entry's two statuses are terminal, and it decides the caching header: `Cache-Control: public, max-age=60` when complete, `no-store` otherwise. The work continues after the request returns, so a `wait=0` read followed by a second read a few seconds later is the cheap way to a complete answer; a warm read within one prediction cycle runs no matcher, no model call and no Journey Planner call. At most four trains per read are worded, soonest first; the rest carry the template under `not_worded` -- past the four-per-read wording cap in this read's soonest-first order, re-evaluated on every read as the trains ahead depart, never cached.

**Byte-identity with the event, and its exact boundary.** When the five fields you pass are verbatim a registration's (a browser's or a webhook subscription's) and the notification pass has already worded that train, the entry serves the pass's own wording and `payload.notification` is byte-identical to the event's. The figures are live where the event's were its mint-time snapshot, and the alternative can differ in one case the operating contract publishes. For any other definition the wording is the read's own draw from a non-deterministic model, or the template. The entry says whether its text is the model's; it never says whether the definition is registered.

**What the read does not do.** No servability caveat (the `coverage` block is what you render an unknown favourite from), no daily cap (nothing is delivered), no decision row -- a definition nobody registered is unscored, deliberately, so nothing here is evidence about alert quality. **Three accepted exposures, published rather than closed**: the completeness and latency of a FIRST read reveal whether a registration with exactly those five fields exists and is alert-worthy now (no status ever says so); the ceiling and allowances above are shared, so one anonymous source at the ceiling holds every caller at 429 and one at the daily wording allowance holds them template-only for the trailing day; and the definition rides in the query string, which the service redacts from its own access log but which any log outside the process may keep.

**After a deploy** the prediction cache is empty for about a minute and the read answers `503 predictions_not_loaded` with `Retry-After`, never an empty list -- an empty list off an empty cache would report an empty process as a calm day. Nothing about the webhook channel's own configuration gates this route: it answers in every environment, store or no store.

parameters.name: from_stop
parameters.description: Boarding stop, `NSR:StopPlace:<digits>`. Canonicalized; the echoed `journey.from_stop` is the ref the answer is about.

parameters.name: to_stop
parameters.description: Alighting stop, `NSR:StopPlace:<digits>`. Must not name the same physical place as `from_stop` after canonicalization.

parameters.name: begin
parameters.description: Period start, `HH:MM` in Europe/Oslo. Given together with `end` or not at all; no period means the whole day (`00:00`-`23:59`).

parameters.name: end
parameters.description: Period end, `HH:MM` in Europe/Oslo, different from `begin`. An `end` before `begin` is a period over midnight -- `22:00`-`01:00` is one read -- and belongs to the weekday it begins on; with no `days` it also asks about yesterday's, which is still open until `end`.

parameters.name: days
parameters.description: Weekdays to ask about, 0 = Monday .. 6 = Sunday, as a REPEATED parameter (`days=0&days=1`) -- a comma-separated list is a 422. Default: today's and tomorrow's Oslo weekday.

parameters.name: wait
parameters.description: Seconds to wait for the wording and the alternative journey before answering. `0` answers at once with whatever is ready; the work continues in the background either way, so read again to complete.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Entries to return. `n_alerts` carries the total and `truncated` says whether the list was cut; the soonest trains are kept.

200.description: The answer, complete or not -- read `complete` and the caching header, which follows it.

Cache-Control.description: `public, max-age=60` when `complete` is true -- a complete answer is safe for an intermediary and for the BFF to hold for a minute -- and `no-store` when it is false, because the incomplete entries change on the next read.

422.description: A malformed definition, period, weekday list, `wait` or `limit`. **Two shapes, and you must handle both.** A refusal this application made -- a ref that is not `NSR:StopPlace:<digits>`, `begin` without `end`, `end` equal to `begin`, a weekday outside 0-6, two refs collapsing to one place -- is `Error`, with `detail` a string that never echoes your value. A refusal the framework made before the handler ran -- `wait` or `limit` out of range, a non-integer `days` element, a comma-separated `days` -- is `ValidationError`, with `detail` an array. `detail`'s type is what tells them apart. A 422 is logged nowhere.

429.description: The read's own limiter -- the global per-minute ceiling or the per-stop-pair one -- answered `rate_limited`. Both are shared by every anonymous caller. `Retry-After` is 60 s. An exhausted wording or Journey Planner allowance is never a 429: it is a per-entry status.

503.description: `predictions_not_loaded` -- the prediction cache has not been loaded since this process started, which is the minute after a deploy -- or `matcher_failed`. Both carry `Retry-After` and both are retryable. Neither has anything to do with the webhook channel's store or credentials, which this route never touches; an empty answer is deliberately never served for either.

get.summary: Every train in a journey definition's window today, graded
get.description:
Every Vy train in today's window on a definition nobody registered, in departure order, each graded: `confirmed` where the outcome is known (ran on time, ran late, cancelled), `predicted` where the model behind `journey-alerts` has a figure, `unknown` where nothing can be said. Built for a glanceable overview of today's commute: one circle per train, filled for a fact and a ring for a forecast.

**No credential**, and the same limiter as `GET /journey-alerts` -- the SAME buckets, global and per canonical stop pair, so reading both routes for one favourite spends the thirty per pair per minute twice as fast.

**The definition** is validated and canonicalized exactly as `journey-alerts` does it, and echoed in `journey`. Only today is answered.

**How old each fact can be** is in `as_of`: the day's timetable (which trains exist, and a cancellation) is rebuilt hourly, the recorded calls every fifteen minutes, the forecasts every prediction cycle. `red` for a forecast is the same bar a notification fires at, applied to the same pairing of a train's two calls. The two reads agree on which forecast trains are bad, with one stated exception: a trip is `cancelled` here when EITHER end is, while notifications fire on the boarding call, so a train cancelled only at your destination is red here and can be absent from `journey-alerts`.

**After a deploy** the timetable is not in memory for the first cycle and the read answers `503 plan_not_loaded` with `Retry-After`, never an empty list.

parameters.name: from_stop
parameters.description: Boarding stop, `NSR:StopPlace:<digits>`. Canonicalized; the echoed `journey.from_stop` is the ref the answer is about.

parameters.name: to_stop
parameters.description: Alighting stop, `NSR:StopPlace:<digits>`. Must not name the same physical place as `from_stop` after canonicalization.

parameters.name: begin
parameters.description: Period start, `HH:MM` in Europe/Oslo. Given together with `end` or not at all; no period means the whole day (`00:00`-`23:59`).

parameters.name: end
parameters.description: Period end, `HH:MM` in Europe/Oslo, different from `begin`. An `end` before `begin` is a period over midnight and belongs to the weekday it begins on; with no `days` it also asks about yesterday's. Until it ends the strip is that night's: at 00:30 it is the window that began at 22:00, and `date` is the day it began. Past midnight, once the plan is rebuilt, trains that arrived before midnight drop out of it.

parameters.name: days
parameters.description: Weekdays the definition travels on, 0 = Monday .. 6 = Sunday, as a REPEATED parameter (`days=0&days=1`). Default: today's and tomorrow's Oslo weekday. Only TODAY is answered; a today not in `days` is an empty list with `reason: not_a_travel_day`.

422.description: A malformed definition, period or weekday list, in the same two shapes as `journey-alerts`: `Error` (a string `detail`) for a refusal this application made, `ValidationError` (an array) for one the framework made -- a non-integer `days` element. A 422 is logged nowhere.

429.description: The limiter shared with `journey-alerts` answered `rate_limited`. `Retry-After` is 60 s.

503.description: `plan_not_loaded` -- the day's timetable has not been loaded since this process started -- or `status_failed`. Both carry `Retry-After` and are retryable; an empty answer is never served for either.

post.summary: An alert about one train on one of your watches
post.description:
Entur POSTs this to your callback destination. The body is `event.schema.json`, referenced here rather than restated.

**Verification.** Each attempt is signed over the exact bytes sent, in the Standard Webhooks shape: HMAC-SHA256 over `webhook-id.webhook-timestamp.<raw body>`, base64, presented as `v1,<signature>`. Verify against the raw body before parsing it. `webhook-id` is stable across attempts of the same delivery, and `webhook-timestamp` and the signature are fresh per attempt -- so a retry that crosses a cycle boundary still lands inside your replay window. Two signature entries are present while a signing generation is being rotated; accept the request if **either** verifies.

**Delivery is at-least-once with no ordering guarantee.** One attempt per notification pass while the event is valid -- validity being the earlier of 60 minutes from `occurred_at`, the train's departure, and the subscription's own lifetime -- after which the event expires and is not retried. The pass period is driven by upstream real-time ingestion rather than a fixed timer, so treat the interval as measured, not promised.

**Suppress before dispatching natively**, in this order: drop a duplicate `event_id`; drop a revision not strictly newer than the highest you have applied for that `alert_id`; and never dispatch a `predicted` revision for a train you have already shown as `confirmed`, whatever its revision. The supplied client package implements all three.

**Answer quickly.** `2xx` is success. `410 Gone` pauses the destination until an operator resumes it, so use it only when you mean "stop for good". `408` and `429` are retried, and a `Retry-After` is honoured up to a cap; other `4xx` are terminal for that event; `5xx` is retried. A redirect is not followed.

parameters.name: webhook-id
parameters.description: The delivery id, stable across attempts. Deduplicate on it as well as on `event_id`.

parameters.name: webhook-timestamp
parameters.description: Unix seconds, fresh per attempt. Reject a timestamp outside your replay window (5 minutes is the reference tolerance).

parameters.name: webhook-signature
parameters.description: Space-delimited `v1,<base64>` entries -- one per live signing generation. Accept if any verifies.

410.description: Gone: pauses this destination until an Entur operator resumes it.

clientKey.description: The credential an Entur operator issued. `Authorization: Bearer kixn_....<secret>`. Never sent as a cookie.

SubscriptionCreate.title: Subscription (request)
SubscriptionCreate.description: The writable half of a subscription. Every property references the authored schema, so a constraint is stated once. The read-only properties -- `client_id`, `version`, `status`, `servable`, `servable_checked_at`, `expires_at`, `created_at`, `updated_at` -- are set by Entur and rejected in a request body.

count.description: How many watches this page holds.

limit.description: The page size that was applied.

next_cursor.description: Pass as `after` to continue. `null` when this is the last page.

CleanupState.title: Cleanup state
CleanupState.description: The auditable completion state of a deletion's second half. `pending` means a repeated `DELETE` will resume it and that expiry is the fallback until it does.

passes.description: How many batched passes this request ran.

residual_hours.description: The maximum window in which anything cleanup did not remove is still stored, after which expiry removes it. Published rather than implied.

existed.description: Whether there was a live watch to tombstone. `false` is not an error.

cleanup.description: `null` when there was nothing to clean up.

retiring.description: Both are valid at once while a rotation is in flight, so accept a request whose signature verifies under either. `null` when nothing is retiring.

Destination.title: Destination
Destination.description: Your callback destination. Carries no signing material: a secret is derived from a root and stored nowhere.

callback_url.description: HTTPS only, default port, no userinfo and no fragment. Provisioned by an operator out of band.

paused.description: Set automatically when your endpoint answers 410; lifted only by an operator.

ready.description: Active, not paused, and signing is configured in this deployment.

TestEventRequest.title: Test event request
TestEventRequest.description: The one place in this document whose property is stated inline instead of referenced. `subscription.schema.json`'s `subscription_id` is the CREATE-side constraint -- your own reference, 128 characters, no `~` -- and it is correctly strict there: a create body must never name the namespaced form. This route accepts that form as well, exactly as the two path routes do, so referencing the create-side definition published a schema that refuses the id an event carries in its own `subscription_id` field. A client validating outbound requests against it would reproduce, in their own client, the 422 this API was fixed to stop returning.

subscription_id.description: A subscription created with `test: true`. Your own reference, or the opaque `subscription_id` an event carries -- the same two forms the path routes accept, and the bound is theirs: `~` plus 128 characters either side. Anything else is refused.

event_id.description: The synthetic event's id, also its `webhook-id`.

status.description: Your endpoint's HTTP status, when it answered at all.

error.description: A short classification of what went wrong, for diagnosis.

signed_generations.description: Which signing generations the attempt was signed under.

JourneyAlerts.title: Journey alerts
JourneyAlerts.description: The trains a notification would go out for on this definition right now, assembled per request from the service's caches. Public and unauthenticated; nothing in it identifies a registration, and no entry ever says whether the definition is registered.

as_of.description: The instant the answer was assembled at, UTC. Every cut in the answer -- departed trains, the windows, "i morgen" -- was made against this one clock.

refreshed_at.description: When the prediction cache the figures come from was loaded. The cache rebuilds only when upstream real-time ingestion moves, so a quiet feed leaves a CORRECT cache old; the age is served rather than refused, and the client judges.

complete.description: Whether every listed entry's `wording.status` and `alternative.status` reached a terminal value. `false` while any is pending or transiently refused; the answer is then `Cache-Control: no-store` and a later read of the same definition completes it.

n_alerts.description: Alert-worthy trains ahead on this definition, before `limit` was applied. Zero means no alert-worthy train AMONG THE TRAINS THE SERVICE SCORES -- direct trips by the operators in `coverage.operators` -- and never all-clear: a trip with a transfer never alerts, and nothing is said about any other operator.

truncated.description: `true` when `limit` cut the list. The soonest trains are the ones kept.

journey.title: Journey definition (echoed)
journey.description: The definition the answer is about, AFTER canonicalization and with the defaults filled in: both refs as the stop registry collapses them, `00:00`-`23:59` when no period was given, today's and tomorrow's Oslo weekday when no `days` were. Key your own cache on this and `refreshed_at`, never on the query string you sent -- two spellings of one place are one answer.

windows.description: The boarding windows the answer covers, as UTC instants: today's remaining window and tomorrow's, on the definition's weekdays, with windows already ended dropped.

coverage.title: Coverage
coverage.description: What the read can and cannot say anything about. It is NOT a servability answer: nothing here says a direct trip runs between the two places today, only that each place is served by something. Render a favourite whose stop is `false` here as unverified rather than calm.

operators.description: The operator codespaces the service scores at all -- Vy rail and the trained bus operators. A train by any other operator is never listed, however disrupted.

from_stop_in_timetable_today.description: Whether the canonical origin appears in TODAY's planned timetable as the service knows it, checked over every ref of the physical place. Fails OPEN: when the timetable is not loaded this reads `true`, because "we do not know" must never be rendered as "not served".

summary.description: One Norwegian sentence over every alert-worthy train ahead -- `n_alerts` of them, not only the listed ones, so a truncated answer reads the same as a full one -- for a favourites row that is skimmed rather than read. The operator's own cause leads when every train's `payload.situations` carry the same operator-written summary (`has_situation` true; a synthetic `KIX:` summary is never quoted as a cause, nor is per-train advice such as «Ta neste tog» or a bare status such as «Forsinket», and since each situation contributes its worst train it is the text that can be shared, never the number): «Signalfeil ved Asker: 4 tog er innstilt og 2 kan bli forsinket». Otherwise the worst train is named as its own `payload.notification.title` names it and the rest are counted per outcome: «Tog L1 07:18 er innstilt, 2 til kan bli forsinket» -- unless another train shares the worst outcome, when the counts stand alone: «4 tog er innstilt, 1 kan bli innstilt og 3 kan bli forsinket». A single train is its title alone. A confirmed and a forecast train never share a verb, and tomorrow's trains are counted apart, with «i dag» said exactly when «i morgen» is («14 tog er innstilt i dag og 2 i morgen»). Built from the figures alone, so it is final at `wait=0` and never waits for wording. `null` when there is nothing to say -- which is never all-clear, for the same reason `n_alerts` of zero is not. Every entry's `payload` carries the same sentence.

summary_en.description: `summary` in English, the same sentence in the same shape («Train L1 07:18 is cancelled, 2 more may be delayed»). The cause leads only when the operator published it in English too; otherwise this line names the trains without it, so the two can differ there and only there. `null` exactly when `summary` is.

summary_nn.description: `summary` in nynorsk, the same sentence in the same shape («Tog L1 07:18 er innstilt, 2 til kan bli forseinka»). The cause leads only once the situation's own `summary_nn` has been translated -- no operator publishes nynorsk, so it is always a machine's -- and otherwise this line names the trains without it, as `summary_en` does. `null` exactly when `summary` is.

alerts.description: Soonest expected departure first, at most `limit` entries.

JourneyAlert.title: Journey alert
JourneyAlert.description: One alert-worthy train ahead. `payload` is EXACTLY the webhook event's payload for this train -- built by the same assembly, referenced here rather than restated -- so a receiver that renders an event renders this. `wording` and `alternative` say where its prose and its alternative journey came from and whether they are final.

severity.description: 1-based rank among this answer's `n_alerts` trains in WORST-FIRST order (the notification pass's own order: severity, then situation number), so a client can re-sort. The list itself is soonest-first, and a truncated answer lists the soonest trains and may therefore lack some ranks.

phase.description: `confirmed` when the real-time feed has declared the train cancelled, or when a Vy train that runs on this weekday is missing from today's timetable altogether (situation `KIX:PlanRemoved:<journey_ref>`) -- a fact, with probabilities of 1.0 and null delay figures in the payload -- else `predicted`. There is no `withdrawn` entry: a train no longer over the gate is simply absent.

train.title: Train
train.description: The train's identity, in the webhook event's own six fields (its `alert_id` is derived from exactly these), so an entry here and an event about the same train join without a translation -- plus `destination` and `mode`, which are not part of that identity.

destination.description: Where the train terminates, as a departure board names it (`Drammen`), and the same value `payload.notification.title` names the train with: «Tog R14 Drammen 14:59». Null when we do not know it, which today is every train but Vy's and every bus.

mode.description: The line's transport mode in the Journey Planner's own `TransportMode` vocabulary (`rail`, `bus`, `metro`, `tram`, `water`, `coach`, ...), the same value as `payload.mode`. It is the LINE's mode, so a replacement bus on a rail line is `rail`. Filter on it to keep a bus favourite's entries to buses, or a train favourite's to trains. Never null for a rail line. For any other line it is null only when the Journey Planner could not be reached as we started, until it answers, normally within a minute.

expected_departure_time.description: Aimed departure plus the typical delay predicted for it -- the figure that decides whether the train can still be caught, and the one the list is ordered on. Equal to the aimed time for a declared cancellation.

source.description: `llm` when `payload.notification` carries the model's prose, `deterministic` when it carries the template. The template is the floor: render it.

status.description: Why the source is what it is. TERMINAL, and held for the situation's life: `ok` (source `llm`), `rejected` and `ungrounded` (the model answered and the answer was unusable for this input -- re-asking would spend a call to learn nothing), `disabled` (this deployment does not deliver the model's prose on this channel, or no backend may be asked -- always so for a train missing from today's timetable, `KIX:PlanRemoved:`, whose text is the template), `not_worded` (past the four-per-read wording cap in this read's soonest-first order, where a `KIX:PlanRemoved:` train takes no place; the template is served, and unlike the rest of this column it is terminal for THIS read only -- re-evaluated on every read as the trains ahead depart, never cached). TRANSIENT, retried on a later read after they expire: `pending` (a background task is writing it), `capped` (the enrichment queue was full), `rate_limited` (the read's own wording allowance is spent), `error` (a transient backend failure).

What became of the alternative-journey lookup behind `payload.alternative_journey`. TERMINAL: `offered` (the payload carries one), `suppressed` (the selection ran and kept the traveller on their own train), `none_found`, `not_worth_lookup` (none was issued -- too far ahead, or below the gate that earns one), `not_looked_up` (past the per-read lookup cap). TRANSIENT, retried after they expire: `pending`, `capped` (queue full), `unanswered` (the Journey Planner did not reply -- throttled, an outage, its cooldown). An `offered` alternative that can no longer be caught is forgotten and looked up again.

Error.title: Error
Error.description:
The shape of every failure THIS APPLICATION refuses: `detail` is a short stable code, not prose to show a traveller, and it deliberately says nothing about another client's records.

**It is not the only failure shape, and a client that assumes it is will throw on the first malformed request it sends.** A request refused before any handler runs -- an unknown body field under `additionalProperties: false`, a value failing its `pattern` or its length or numeric bound, a missing required property, a path segment over its bound, a body that is not an object -- is refused by the framework, whose `detail` is an ARRAY: see `ValidationError`. That is why every 422 documented here is a `oneOf` of the two, and why `GET`/`DELETE` routes that constrain a parameter document a 422 at all.

ValidationError.title: Validation error
ValidationError.description:
FastAPI's own refusal, for a request no handler here ever saw. `detail` is an **array of objects** (`type`/`loc`/`msg`/`input`, plus `ctx` where the violated constraint has a value to quote), never a string -- so test `detail`'s type before reading it as one.

**Published rather than flattened, deliberately.** Reshaping these into `Error` needs a `RequestValidationError` handler, and FastAPI registers those per APPLICATION, not per router: this API is mounted in a process that also serves `/varsel-api`, `/historikk-api`, `/meldinger-api` and more, so one handler would silently restate every one of their validation bodies too. Two honest shapes beat one uniform shape bought at that price. `docs/integrations/notification-api.md` says the same thing in prose.

The item's key set is Pydantic's rather than ours, so it is deliberately left open here. Measured against this app (FastAPI 0.140, Pydantic 2.13) over a query bound, a query type, a path length, a body pattern, a missing field, a forbidden extra field and a non-object body: every item carried `type`, `loc`, `msg` and `input`, and `ctx` appeared on the four that had a constraint to name.

type.description: Pydantic's error kind: `missing`, `extra_forbidden`, `string_pattern_mismatch`, `string_too_long`, `less_than_equal`, `int_parsing`, `model_attributes_type`, and others. Match on this rather than on `msg`.

loc.description: Where the offending value sits: `["query", "limit"]`, `["path", "subscription_id"]`, `["body", "from_stop"]`, or `["body"]` for a body that is not an object. An INTEGER element is an index into an array property -- `["body", "days", 1]` -- which is why the items are string or integer and not string.

msg.description: English prose from Pydantic. For your log, not for a traveller: it is neither Norwegian nor a stable code.

input.description: The value that was refused, as received -- any JSON type, and for `missing` it is the enclosing object. Required, and on the same footing as the three beside it: Pydantic declares `type`, `loc`, `msg` and `input` always present and `ctx` optional, and all seven refusals measured against this app agreed.

ctx.description: The constraint that was violated, when the error kind has one to quote: `{"le": 500}`, `{"max_length": 257}`, `{"pattern": "^[A-Za-z0-9._:~-]+$"}`. Absent for kinds with no constraint, such as `missing`.

JourneyStatus.title: Journey status
JourneyStatus.description: Every Vy train in today's window on the definition, in departure order, each graded. Built per request from memory the service already holds; nothing in it identifies a registration.

now.description: The instant the answer was assembled at, UTC. Draw the «now» marker against this, not against the device clock.

date.description: The Oslo date the window is on.

window.description: Today's `[begin, end]` as UTC instants, the past half included; null on a day not in `days`.

reason.description: `not_a_travel_day` when today is not in `days`, else null.

operators.description: Operators whose trains are listed: `["VYG"]`. A trip by any other operator is never listed.

as_of.description: When each source was loaded. The day's timetable is rebuilt hourly and the recorded calls every fifteen minutes, so a cancellation or a recorded arrival can be that old.

actuals_refreshed_at.description: Today's recorded calls; null until they are loaded, when the timetable's own recorded calls stand in.

journey.title: Journey definition (echoed)
journey.description: The definition the answer is about, AFTER canonicalization and with the defaults filled in: both refs as the stop registry collapses them, `00:00`-`23:59` when no period was given, today's and tomorrow's Oslo weekday when no `days` were. Key your own cache on this and `refreshed_at`, never on the query string you sent -- two spellings of one place are one answer.

coverage.title: Coverage
coverage.description: What the read can and cannot say anything about. It is NOT a servability answer: nothing here says a direct trip runs between the two places today, only that each place is served by something. Render a favourite whose stop is `false` here as unverified rather than calm.

operators.description: The operators this answer covers -- `["VYG"]`, the same as the top-level `operators`.

from_stop_in_timetable_today.description: Whether the canonical origin appears in TODAY's planned timetable as the service knows it, checked over every ref of the physical place. Fails OPEN: when the timetable is not loaded this reads `true`, because "we do not know" must never be rendered as "not served".

summary.description: journey-alerts' `summary`: one sentence over the alert-worthy trains on this definition right now, from the same figures. Not over `trains`: it can count tomorrow's trains, which this read does not list. `null` when there is nothing to say, and also when the predictions are not loaded or the matcher failed -- the trains are served regardless.

TrainStatus.title: Train status
TrainStatus.description: One Vy train in today's window that boards at the origin and lets you off at the destination.

departure_time.description: Aimed departure from the boarding stop, UTC.

arrival_time.description: Aimed arrival at the alighting stop, UTC.

destination.description: Where the train terminates, as a departure board names it (`Hamar`); name the train with it: `RE10 Hamar 08:00`. Null when the plan does not say.

mode.description: The line's transport mode in the Journey Planner's `TransportMode` vocabulary, as on journey-alerts: `rail` for every train listed today.

jkey.description: The dated journey ref with its codespace stripped.

state.description: `confirmed` when the alighting call is recorded, or the train is cancelled and its aimed departure has passed; a recorded call outranks an earlier cancellation, so a reinstated train that ran reads as run -- draw it filled. `predicted` when the model has a figure (or the cancellation is announced but not yet due) -- draw a ring. `unknown` when nothing can be said, including a train with no operator message more than two hours out, whose score is not better than the base rate.

level.description: `red` cancelled, 10 min or more late, or (predicted) over the same alert bar a notification fires at; `yellow` 5-9 min; `green` less; `grey` exactly when `state` is `unknown` or a confirmed train has no delay figure.

cancelled.description: The boarding or the alighting call is cancelled -- a partial cancellation that cuts your stretch counts.

delay_min.description: Confirmed delay at the alighting stop, minutes; null unless `state` is `confirmed`.

expected_departure_time.description: Aimed departure plus the typical predicted departure delay; null unless `state` is `predicted`.

delay_p50_min.description: Typical predicted arrival delay, minutes; null unless `state` is `predicted`.

impact_probability.description: P(cancelled OR 10 min or more late) at the boarding stop, the figure notifications are gated on. 1.0 for a cancellation. Null on a confirmed or unknown train, and on a forecast scored at only one end of the trip -- notifications cannot fire on one, so neither is it red.

alert_worthy.description: Whether this forecast clears the bar a notification would fire at; true for a cancellation, false for every confirmed or unknown train.

observed_at.description: Aimed time of the call a confirmed figure was read off, UTC -- how old the fact is.

removed_from_plan.description: The train is missing from today's timetable altogether: Vy runs it on this weekday, today's plan does not have it, and no cancellation has been published. Always `cancelled` and `red` too, drawn by the same ring-then-fill rule -- but say «tatt ut av rutetabellen» rather than «innstilt», since a traveller who checks the operator's own channels will find no cancellation.

bus_for_train.description: A removed train the operator has set up a replacement bus for; false on every other train.

Unauthorized.description: Missing, unknown, revoked, expired or wrong credential. The body says which it is not.

Suspended.description: The credential is valid and the client is suspended. Not a credential to rotate.

NotFound.description: No such record for this credential. Missing, deleted, expired and another client's are one answer.

Unprocessable.description: The request body is malformed. **Two shapes, and you must handle both.** A refusal this application made -- a bad window, weekday set or stop pair, an unknown `destination_id` -- is `Error`, with `detail` a string. A refusal the framework made before the handler ran -- an unknown property, a value failing its pattern or bound, a missing required property -- is `ValidationError`, with `detail` an array. `detail`'s type is what tells them apart.

ValidationFailed.description: A parameter or body property failed its published schema, and no handler here ran. Only the framework's array shape reaches you on this route: it has no refusal of its own at this status.

RateLimited.description: A limiter tier or a quota ceiling. `Retry-After` is always present and bounded.

Unavailable.description: The webhook channel is not configured in this deployment, or its store is briefly unavailable. Retryable, and not a statement about your credential.

ET-Client-Name.name: ET-Client-Name
ET-Client-Name.description: Who is calling, as `<company>-<application>` (lowercase, no spaces) -- the header Entur asks of every consumer of its APIs. The public reads record it on their log record so the team can reach a caller about its traffic; a value outside `[A-Za-z0-9._-]{1,64}` is recorded as `invalid`. It never changes the answer or the rate limits.
